👑🌱 LEADERSHIP IS ABOUT LIFTING OTHERS

One of the greatest lessons I’ve learned about leadership is this:

Being a leader isn’t about showing off.

It isn’t about shaming people.

It isn’t about embarrassing people.

It isn’t about pushing someone else down so you can climb higher. 🚫

And it certainly isn’t about making people feel small so that you can feel powerful.

Real leadership is about leveling up others. 📈🤝

A great leader looks around and asks:

🧭 How can I help you grow?

📚 What can I teach you?

🎙️ How can I help you find your voice?

🌱 How can I create an opportunity for you?

🏆 How can I celebrate your success without feeling threatened by it?

Because when you help somebody else rise, their success doesn’t diminish yours.

It multiplies the impact.

That’s something I began learning as a child.

The microphone taught me to use my voice. 🎙️

The classroom taught me to keep learning. 📚

The teachers taught me that knowledge can be shared. 👩🏽‍🏫

And life taught me that leadership comes with responsibility. ⚖️

Today, I believe the highest form of leadership isn’t standing at the top saying,

“Look how high I am.”

It’s standing beside someone and saying,

“Come on. I’ll help you get there too.” 🤝✨

That’s leadership.

Not domination.

Not humiliation.

Not competition for attention.

Elevation.

🌱 Grow people.

🧠 Develop people.

❤️ Encourage people.

🎓 Teach people.

🎙️ Give people a voice.

🏆 Celebrate their victories.

Because the strongest leaders don’t create followers who remain beneath them.

They develop people who become leaders themselves.

🗼 Build the lighthouse—not to stand above everyone else, but to help others see their way forward.

content:
Liderlik Dediğin...
Rakamlardan ibaret değildir tabela.
Cirolar, hedefler, çeyrek raporları geçer gider. Geride ne kaldığına bakarsın.
Gerçek liderlik;
En tepedeki koltuğa oturduğunda, başladığı ilk günü unutmamaktır.
Mutfağın tozunu yutmuş olmaktır.
30 yıllık tecrübenin üzerine basıp yükselmek değil; o tecrübeyi etrafındakilere basamak yapabilmektir.
Geçenlerde bir yönetim felsefesi takıldı aklıma.
Bir lider düşünün.
Şirketin en kıdemli emektarını sahneye çıkarıp, "Ben değil, onun 35 yıllık birikimi bizi biz yaptı" diyebiliyor.
Aynı lider, masanın diğer tarafına geçip şirkete henüz dün adım atmış gençlerle kahvaltı yapıyor.
Neden mi?
Alışkanlık körlüğüne teslim olmamak için.
"Biz bu işi yıllardır böyle yapıyoruz" ezberini bozmak için.
İşte vizyon dediğin tam olarak budur.
Eğer bir yönetici;
Ömrünü o kuruma vermiş bir usta çınarın hakkını teslim ediyorsa,
Ve aynı zamanda gencecik bir zihnin "Neden?" sorusuna kulak veriyorsa…
Orada sadece bir şirket yönetilmiyordur.
Orada bir kültür inşa ediliyordur.
Kendi ışığını saçarken etrafındakilerin de parlamasına müsaade eden,
İnsana yatırım yapmayı en büyük yatırım sayan,
Geçmişin tecrübesiyle geleceğin tazeliğini aynı masada buluşturan tüm liderlere selam olsun.
Çünkü biliriz ki;
Koltuğun gücü geçicidir.
Dokunduğun hayatlar, bıraktığın izler kalıcıdır.



What Leadership Truly Means…
​Success is never just about numbers on a board.
​Revenue figures, quarterly goals, financial projections they all fade over time. In the end, what truly matters is what remains.
​Real leadership is simple:
When you reach the top seat, it’s about never forgetting where you started.
It’s having worked on the front lines and carrying that experience with you.
It’s not stepping on 30 years of accumulated wisdom to climb higher, but turning that wisdom into a stepping stone for everyone around you.
​A specific management philosophy came to mind recently.
​Picture a leader.
One who brings the most senior veteran of the company onto the stage and says, "It isn't just me; his 35 years of dedication made us who we are today."
Then, that same leader walks over to sit with young professionals who just joined yesterday.
​Why?
To refuse complacency.
To shatter the lazy excuse of, "Well, we’ve always done it this way."
​That is true vision.
​When an executive honors the legacy of a master who gave a lifetime to the organization, while actively listening to a young mind asking "Why?"they aren't just managing a company.
​They are building a culture.
​Here’s to the leaders who let others shine while spreading their own light,
Who treat investing in people as the highest form of growth,
And who bring the wisdom of experience and the energy of fresh perspectives to the exact same table.
​Because position and power are temporary.
The lives you touch and the legacy you leave are permanent.

🌱 Leadership is changing — and so is the meaning of success.

Every generation enters the workplace with different expectations, different strengths, and a different definition of what matters.

Today, being a good leader is no longer just about having a senior position, giving instructions, or making decisions.

It is about adapting, listening, learning, and helping others grow. 🤝

The newer generation is entering a world shaped by AI, automation, changing work cultures, global opportunities, and constant uncertainty. At the same time, they are also bringing something valuable — curiosity, new perspectives, digital adaptability, and the courage to question old ways of working. 💡

But there is one thing every generation can learn from each other:

🔹 Experience teaches us what has worked before.
🔹 Innovation challenges us to think about what could work next.
🔹 Leadership brings both together.

A strong leader doesn't try to create people who think exactly like them.

A strong leader creates an environment where people can think, question, contribute, and become better than they were yesterday. 🚀

As we begin another Monday, perhaps leadership is not about asking:

"How can I get ahead ?"

But rather:

"How can I move forward while helping others move forward too ?" 🌍

Because careers may change, technologies may change, and generations may change — but the value of good leadership, continuous learning, and human connection will never go out of style.

Wishing everyone a meaningful and productive Monday. ☕📈

Likhita Karanam

ABŞ Dövlət Departamentinin Beynəlxalq Ziyarətçi Liderlik Proqramı (International Visitor Leadership Program – IVLP) çərçivəsində bir ay davam edən işgüzar səfərim başa çatdı. Proqramı başa vurmağım münasibətilə Amerika Birləşmiş Ştatlarının Azərbaycandakı səfirliyində təşkil olunan görüşdə mənə  xüsusi və mənim üçün çox dəyərli olan sertifikat təqdim olundu.Bir vaxtlar müxtəlif ölkə rəhbərlərinin və nüfuzlu şəxslərin də qatıldığı bu əhəmiyyətli proqrama Azərbaycandan məhz məni seçdiklərinə görə Amerika Birləşmiş Ştatlarının Azərbaycandakı səfirliyinə, o cümlədən səfərin təşkilində  göstərdikləri böyük dəstəyə  görə səfirlik əməkdaşları dəyərli Fatimə Həsənovaya və Fərqan Əliyevə dərin təşəkkürümü bildirirəm. Bu bir ay ərzində Amerikanı sanki yenidən kəşf etdim. Tarixi, memarlığı, möhtəşəm təbiəti, zəngin mədəniyyəti, fərqli həyat tərzi, tolerantlığı və qonaqpərvər insanları ilə ABŞ məndə həyata yeni bir baxış formalşdırdı.Müxtəlif xalqları və dini icmaları təmsil edən insanlarla keçirdiyim görüşlər, rəsmi şəxslərlə apardığım fikir mübadilələri, yeni tanışlıqlar və dostluqlar həyat kitabımda yeni və maraqlı bir səhifə açdı. Ziyarət etdiyim müxtəlif profilli muzeylər isə bu səfərin ən yaddaqalan məqamlarından biri oldu.
Bu səfər zamanı qazandığım bilikləri, topladığım təcrübəni gələcək fəaliyyətimdə tətbiq etməyə səbirsizlənirəm. Eyni zamanda, səfərim zamanı Azərbaycana dəvət etdiyim dəyərli insanların ölkəmizdə qonaq olacağı günü səbirsizliklə gözləyirəm.
Hər şey üçün çox sağ ol, əziz Amerika!
Biz yenə görüşəcəyik!

My month-long professional visit to the United States under the U.S. Department of State’s International Visitor Leadership Program (IVLP) has come to an end.

To mark the completion of the program, I was presented with a special certificate—one that is particularly meaningful and valuable to me—at a meeting organized at the U.S. Embassy in Azerbaijan.

I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the U.S. Embassy in Azerbaijan for selecting me to represent Azerbaijan in this important program, which over the years has brought together heads of state and many distinguished individuals from around the world. I am also deeply grateful to the wonderful Embassy staff members, Fatima Hasanova and Farqan Aliyev, for their tremendous support and contribution to the organization of this journey.

Over the course of this month, I felt as though I had discovered America all over again. Its history, architecture, breathtaking nature, rich culture, unique way of life, spirit of tolerance, and welcoming people have given me a new perspective on life.

Meetings with people representing different nations and religious communities, exchanges of ideas with officials, new acquaintances and friendships—all of these experiences have opened a new and fascinating chapter in the book of my life. Visiting museums of many different kinds was also among the most memorable highlights of this journey.
Thank you for everything, dear America! We will meet again!

Mükemmel Mentörlük, "Senin Bile Görmediğin" Potansiyelini Sana Göstermektir

​Kurumlarda yöneticileri ve öğretmenleri geliştirirken en büyük engellerden biri, kişilerin kendi zayıflıklarının ve hatta güçlü yönlerinin farkında olmamasıdır. Psikologlar Luft ve Ingham'ın yarattığı meşhur "Johari Penceresi", liyakatli insan kaynağı inşasının en güçlü aracıdır.

​Johari Penceresinde en tehlikeli bölge "Kör Alan"dır: Sizin kendi hakkınızda bilmediğiniz, ancak dışarıdan ekibinizin veya liderinizin net bir şekilde gördüğü eksiklikler veya potansiyeller.

​Denetçi ruhlu bir yönetici, çalışanın kör alanındaki hatayı bulur ve bunu bir ceza aracı olarak kullanır. 
Usta bir mentör ise; radikal bir şeffaflıkla o kör noktaya ayna tutar, "Sende o stratejik zekayı görüyorum ama mikro-yönetim yaparak kendi potansiyelini boğuyorsun" der. 
Gerçek liderlik; insanların kör alanlarını küçültüp, açık (potansiyel) alanlarını devasa boyutlara ulaştırma sanatıdır. İnsanları eleştirmeyin, onları kendileriyle tanıştırın.

​***

Perfect Mentorship is Showing You the Potential "Even You Don't See"

​When developing managers and teachers in institutions, one of the biggest obstacles is that individuals are unaware of their own weaknesses and even their strengths. The famous "Johari Window," created by psychologists Luft and Ingham, is the most powerful tool for building competent human resources.

​The most dangerous zone in the Johari Window is the "Blind Spot": The flaws or potentials about yourself that you do not know, but your team or leader clearly sees from the outside.

​A manager with an auditor spirit finds the mistake in the employee's blind spot and uses it as a tool for punishment. A master mentor, however, holds a mirror to that blind spot with radical transparency and says, "I see that strategic intelligence in you, but you are suffocating your own potential by micro-managing." True leadership is the art of shrinking people's blind spots and expanding their open (potential) areas to massive dimensions. Don't criticize people; introduce them to themselves.

Strong leaders don’t just ask, “What’s next?”

There are moments in leadership when moving forward begins with reflection.

Not everything needs to change.

And not everything needs to stay.

The work is having the wisdom to discern:

• What should we preserve?
• What should we strengthen?
• What are we ready to release?

Because if we hold onto everything, we leave very little room for what’s possible.

Letting go doesn’t mean disregarding what came before. It means honoring what has served us, learning from it, and recognizing when making room allows something new to emerge.

That is true for people.

It is true for leaders.

And it is true for organizations.

Leadership isn’t about changing everything. It’s about knowing what to honor, what to strengthen, and what to release.

Reflect. Learn. Make room.

content:
💯🎯✔ WHO IS RESPONSIBLE WHEN SOMEONE ON YOUR TEAM CAN NO LONGER CARRY THE LOAD?

Leader A:

"Everyone is responsible for themselves. People need to solve their own problems."

Leader B:

"Strong teams step forward when one person can no longer carry the burden alone."

Who is closer to the truth?

A mother stork was killed by high-voltage power lines.

She left behind four chicks too young to survive on their own.

The father stayed.

He protected them.

But he couldn't feed them all by himself.

Then something unexpected happened.

People from a nearby village noticed the struggle.

Instead of walking away...

They stepped in.

Day after day, they brought food to the nest until the young birds became strong enough to fly.

It made me think about leadership.

The strongest organizations aren't built because everyone is always strong.

They're built because people know when to carry one another.

Every team will eventually face a season when someone loses capacity.

A family crisis.

A health challenge.

A personal setback.

A professional disappointment.

In those moments...

Leadership isn't measured by policies.

It's measured by compassion.

Because people rarely forget the organization that stood beside them when they couldn't stand alone.

🎁 BONUS 1

Leadership isn't only about achieving results.

It's about recognizing when people need support to achieve them.

🎁 BONUS 2

Strong cultures are built long before a crisis.

A crisis simply reveals whether the culture is real.

🎁 BONUS 3

Great leaders don't ask,

"Who should fix this?"

They ask,

"How can we help this person succeed again?"

🤔 Debate:

Should organizations provide extra support when employees face personal hardship...

Or should everyone be expected to carry their own responsibilities regardless of circumstances?

Where do you think the balance should be?

Share your experience.

header.text: New post in Brain Expansion Group

content:
Be careful judging how someone handles pressure when you’ve never had to survive their kind of heat.

Two people can walk into the same room, work the same job, face the same challenge—and experience it completely differently.

Because you’re only seeing this moment.

You don’t see what happened before they arrived.

You don’t know what they’re carrying home.

You don’t know how many times they’ve already had to be strong.

And you definitely don’t know how close someone may be to their breaking point.

That’s why great leadership requires more than standards and accountability.

It requires emotional intelligence.

You can hold people accountable without humiliating them.

You can correct someone without destroying their confidence.

You can disagree without becoming disrespectful.

And you can be strong without becoming cold.

Before you judge someone’s reaction, remember:

Everybody carries a story you cannot see.

Lead with grace.
Lead with understanding.
Lead with humanity.

Because sometimes people don’t need you to lower the standard.

They just need you to understand the pressure. 🧊🔥

content:
🌍 1800’den 2026’ya kadar dünyada yaklaşık 20 milyar insan doğdu.

Bir an durup düşünelim…

Bu insanların arasında çalışanlar, yöneticiler, girişimciler, liderler, mühendisler, öğretmenler, doktorlar, üreticiler ve dünyayı değiştiren insanlar vardı.

Kimi şirketler kurdu.
Kimi binlerce insana liderlik etti.
Kimi kariyerinin zirvesine ulaştı.
Kimi ise ailesi ve sevdikleri için her gün mücadele etti.

Hepsinin hedefleri, planları, başarıları ve endişeleri vardı.

Ve sonunda hepsi bir hayat hikâyesine dönüştü.

Bugün biz de bu büyük insanlık hikâyesinin bir parçasıyız.

💼 Kariyerimiz önemli.
📈 Başarılarımız önemli.
👥 Liderliğimiz ve insanlara kattığımız değer önemli.

Ama belki de en önemlisi, bize verilen zamanı nasıl kullandığımız.

Kariyerimizi inşa ederken hayatımızı da kaçırmayalım.

Çünkü unvanlarımız bir gün unutulabilir;
ama insanlara kattığımız değer ve arkamızda bıraktığımız etki yaşamaya devam eder.

⸻

🌎 Approximately 20 billion people were born between 1800 and 2026.

Think about that for a moment…

Among them were employees, managers, entrepreneurs, leaders, engineers, teachers, doctors, creators and people who changed the world.

Some built companies.
Some led thousands of people.
Some reached the top of their careers.
Others simply worked hard every day for their families and loved ones.

They all had goals, plans, achievements and worries.

And eventually, every one of them became a life story.

Today, we are also part of this enormous human story.

💼 Our careers matter.
📈 Our achievements matter.
👥 Our leadership and the value we create for others matter.

But perhaps what matters most is how we use the time we have been given.

Let’s build our careers without forgetting to build our lives.

Because our titles may one day be forgotten,
but the value we add to people and the impact we leave behind can last.

Better people. Better workplaces. A brighter future. 🌍

Leadership isn’t just about knowing what you’re allowed to do.

It’s about knowing when your choices affect the people around you.

You can have the freedom to do something and still choose not to, because you understand the impact it could have on someone else.

That’s not weakness.

That’s maturity.

Great leaders:
• Don’t lead through legalism or control
• Think beyond their own preferences
• Put the growth of others ahead of their own comfort

Sometimes leadership means saying:

“I could do this, but I won’t if it could hurt the people I’m responsible for.”

Freedom without responsibility is selfishness.

Freedom guided by responsibility is leadership.

content:
I think one of the most important traits of a lead is the willingness to accept responsibility when things go wrong.

It's easy to stand in front of a team when everything goes right and accept the credit.

Leadership gets tested when it doesn't.

A good lead doesn't immediately look for someone to blame. They ask, “What could I have done differently? What did I miss? What should I have caught?”

Sometimes accepting responsibility means sacrificing a little face. It means admitting that you made the wrong call, didn't communicate well enough, or should have seen a problem coming.

Taking responsibility doesn't make a leader weak.

It makes them worthy.

Your team needs to know that you'll stand in front of them when things go wrong just as readily as you'll stand in front of them when things go right.

You're willingness to accept responsibility for the failures is how you earn your right to share in the success.

That's leadership. 🫡

content:
Leaders, remember: iron sharpens iron.
Leadership is more than managing performance, meeting goals, or holding people accountable. It’s also about developing people.
Coach your team. Challenge them. Empower them to make decisions. Support them when they stumble, and recognize them when they succeed.
Don’t be intimidated when someone on your team is talented, ambitious, or full of new ideas. Develop them. Great leaders don’t dim someone else’s light to protect their own position. They help people become stronger, more confident, and prepared for their next level.
Lead with a servant mentality. Ask yourself: What does my team need from me to be successful?
Sometimes it’s direction. Sometimes it’s accountability. Sometimes it’s an opportunity. And sometimes they need to know their leader believes in them.
Your leadership should leave people better than you found them.
Build leaders, not followers. Because when your people grow, your organization grows with them. 💙

content:
Unpopular opinion: Not every good employee wants to become a manager.
We talk about promotions like management is the natural next step in everyone’s career.
You’re good at your job?
“Maybe you should become a Team Leader.”
You’re experienced?
“You should manage a team.”
But honestly, some people are excellent at what they do and have absolutely no interest in managing people.
And that’s okay.
Being a great individual contributor doesn’t mean you’ll automatically be a great manager.
Managing people means dealing with conflicts, difficult conversations, different personalities, performance issues, expectations, and a hundred things that have nothing to do with the job you were originally good at.
Some people want to become leaders.
Some want to become specialists.
Some simply want to become really, really good at their profession.
We shouldn’t make people feel like they are “not ambitious” just because they don't want to manage a team.
Career growth doesn't have one direction.
Sometimes the best career move is not moving into management.
What do you think?
#UnpopularOpinion #CareerGrowth #Leadership #HR #Workplace

content:
What's the difference between management and leadership? Are they really different? Or are they really the same? 

I've heard this discussion time and time again, and how it's articulated differs from one person to the next. For me, a simple framework to help distinguish the differences and the overlaps can be outlined in a vin diagram. 

Management concerns itself with the "how" and "when" of the work - in other words, the process and execution. 

Leadership concerns itself with the "where" and the "why" - or, in other words, the purpose and vision of an organization. 

And they both come together to determine the "who" and the "what" - or the people and the results. 

Maybe that's too simplistic and ignores the nuanced differences. Maybe it ignores the biggest differentiating functions of a manager or a leader. 

What do you think?

content:
Leadership vs. Management: Why Both Matter

Leadership and management are often used interchangeably, but they are not the same.

Leadership is about setting a vision, inspiring people, building trust, and influencing others to move toward a common goal.

Management is about planning, organizing, coordinating resources, setting processes, and ensuring that tasks and goals are achieved efficiently.

Simply put:

🔹 Leaders inspire.
🔹 Managers organize.
🔹 Leaders focus on people and direction.
🔹 Managers focus on processes and execution.

But here’s the important part: organizations need both.

A great leader without effective management may have a strong vision but struggle with execution. Likewise, a good manager without leadership may maintain processes but fail to inspire and develop people.

The strongest organizations combine effective leadership with strong management to achieve sustainable growth and build high-performing teams.

Leadership gives the direction. Management makes the direction achievable.

Managing people is probably one of the biggest parts of my job — and also one of the parts I enjoy the most.

For me, good management isn’t about having all the answers, giving instructions or being the loudest person in the room.
It’s about understanding people.

Knowing when someone needs pushing, when they need supporting, when they need more responsibility and sometimes when they just need someone to listen.

Everyone is different, and getting the best out of a team means giving people the confidence and environment to actually be themselves at work.

I’m lucky to work alongside some brilliant supervisors and team members, and one of the things I’m most proud of is seeing people grow in confidence, take ownership and start backing themselves.

Of course, we still have targets to hit, standards to maintain and plenty of stressful days — but I’ve always believed people perform better when they actually enjoy coming to work.

Create a good environment, look after your people, challenge them when they need it, recognise them when they deserve it, and usually the results follow.

content:
Managing people and developing people are not the same job.

That is a lesson I had to learn through experience.

You can give somebody a task, set a deadline, check their work, and technically be managing them.

Development requires more.

It means helping people understand the standard.

It means explaining the reason behind the work instead of only giving instructions.

It means creating enough room for someone to make decisions, learn from mistakes, build confidence, and eventually operate without needing you involved in every step.

As a manager, one of my goals is not simply to have a team that performs well when I am present.

I want people to become stronger professionals because they were part of my team.

That changes the way I approach feedback, performance conversations, goal setting, and even accountability.

Sometimes leadership means correcting something.

Sometimes it means coaching.

Sometimes it means getting out of the way because the person you developed is ready to own it.

The goal should never be dependence on the manager.

The goal is capacity.

Governance and management are not interchangeable. 🚫 
And confusing the two can create a serious organizational problem:
Everyone is busy, but nobody is really governing. 🤦‍♀️ 

Management asks:
✔️ How do we get the work done?
Governance asks:
✔️ Are we doing the right things, in the right way, for the right reasons?
Management focuses on:
* execution
* resources
* processes
* activities
* performance
Governance focuses on:
* direction
* accountability
* decision-making
* oversight
* integrity
* long-term sustainability
Both are necessary.
But they serve different purposes. 😉 
A manager may decide how a process should operate.
Governance should ensure that the decision:
✔️ supports organizational objectives,
✔️ respects applicable requirements,
✔️ considers risks,
✔️ has appropriate accountability,
✔️ and serves the organization's purpose.
When governance is weak, management can become very efficient at moving in the wrong direction. 🤕 

In your organization, do you think governance and management are clearly distinguished—or often mixed together? 🎙️ 🎙️ 🎙️

A Manager Can Run a Hotel. A Leader Can Change It.

Over the years in the hotel industry, I’ve learned that there is a difference between managing people and leading people.

A manager can make schedules, monitor numbers, enforce policies, and make sure the operation gets through the day.

A leader does something deeper.

A leader walks into the lobby and notices the employee who is struggling. A leader recognizes when a guest needs more than a solution they need someone to genuinely care. A leader doesn't simply tell a team what to do; they show them why it matters.

I’ve always believed that hospitality starts with people.

When I lead, I don't expect my team to give a level of service that I wouldn't give myself. I believe in being present, listening, coaching, holding people accountable, and most importantly, helping people see what they are capable of becoming.

Some of the moments I'm most proud of in my career aren't found on a balance sheet or a performance report. They're in the people I've had the opportunity to mentor watching team members gain confidence, take on greater responsibility, and eventually step into leadership themselves.

That's the part of hospitality that means the most to me.

Management is about getting the job done. Leadership is about developing the people who will carry the job forward.

Hotels are built with rooms, systems, and processes but  great hotels are built by people who feel valued, empowered, and inspired to serve.

That's the kind of leader I strive to be.

Management Is More Than Processes and Numbers

Management is often associated with processes, indicators, budgets and results. All of these are important—but they are only part of the picture.

Behind every result, there are people making decisions, solving problems, dealing with unexpected situations and creating value.

A well-designed process can improve efficiency, but it is people who make that process work. Likewise, data can support better decisions, but it still takes judgment to understand the context and determine what should be done.

This is why effective management requires a balance between efficiency, analytical thinking and the human side of organizations.

Good management is not simply about achieving a target. It is about understanding how the different elements of an organization work together to create sustainable results.
In the end, numbers tell us what happened. Management also needs to understand why it happened—and what should happen next.

Change Management: Employees Don’t Resist Change. They Resist Feeling Out of Control.

Why do new systems, organizational restructuring, and major process changes so often face resistance?

It’s easy to blame employees for being unwilling to adapt.

But the reality is more complicated.

People naturally resist change because change disrupts familiarity and introduces uncertainty.

When people don’t know what’s coming next, they can feel like they’re losing control.

That’s why successful change management isn’t just about explaining why the company needs to change.

It’s also about helping employees understand:

“What does this change mean for me?”

Effective leaders make the transition easier by providing:

🎯 Clear communication

Explain what is changing, why it is happening, and what employees can expect.

📚 Proper training

Give people the skills and confidence they need to succeed in the new environment.

⏳ A reasonable transition period

Not everyone adapts at the same speed. Give people enough time to learn, adjust, and build confidence.

👂 A genuine opportunity to be heard

Listen to concerns instead of immediately dismissing them as resistance.

Because change management isn’t simply about managing processes.

It’s about managing uncertainty, emotions, and trust.

People are much more likely to embrace change when they feel informed, supported, and involved in the process.

The best leaders don’t force people through change.

They help people feel confident enough to move through it.

I get the sense we’re all noticing this.

Leadership is what happens when we meet people and help things move.

So perhaps the better questions aren’t:
“How do we lead.”
or
“How do we manage.”

But:
“What are we meeting.”

Meet the people.
Meet the work.
Meet reality.

Stop Leading. Stop Managing. Start Meeting.

content:
Back from Summer vacacion, Rethinking How We Design Work.

After a restorative summer break filled with books, museums, concerts, conversations, long walks and moments of genuine disconnection, I found myself reflecting on a paradox that many global organizations continue to face:
We have more employee data than ever before yet seem less capable of understanding the real human experience of work.
Perhaps the challenge is not a lack of metrics, but a lack of integration between human factors, organizational systems and leadership accountability.
In my latest article, I explore what I call the Industrial Psychosocial Scaffold: a framework that connects psychosocial risk management, cognitive ergonomics and local leadership accountability to help organizations design sustainable performance at scale.
As AI, digitalization and increasing complexity reshape work, the question is no longer how to optimize performance.
It is how to sustain human capability over time.

content:
Change Made Easy | Episode 8

Not every workplace change is a major transformation.

Sometimes it's a new system. Sometimes it's a new process. A restructure. A new leader. A policy change. A merger.  A new way of working.

And sometimes it's simply telling people:
"Starting Monday, we're doing this differently." 

Big or small, here's what I've learned: if the change affects how people work, it needs to be managed.

A few ways to make change easier:
→ Identify who is impacted. Please don't wait until go-live to figure this out.
→ Explain the WHY. "Because management decided" is not a change strategy.
→ Listen early. Resistance can tell you where the gaps are.
→ Equip your managers. Your people will probably ask them before they ask anyone else.
→ Communicate more than once. Sending the email ≠ managing the change.
→ Check adoption. Go-live tells you the solution was implemented. It doesn't tell you the change worked.

Again, Change doesn't have to be complicated.

Sometimes it's simply being intentional about the people who have to do something differently tomorrow because of a decision we made today.

Make the change. Manage the impact. Bring the people with you.





#ChangeMadeEasy #OrganizationalChangeManagement #ChangeLeadership #Leadership #BusinessTransformation #OCM

People Management: Management vs. Leadership

One of the biggest lessons I’ve learned about people management is that being a manager and being a leader are not the same thing.

Management is about the work:
• Setting expectations
• Creating processes
• Tracking performance
• Meeting deadlines
• Holding people accountable

Leadership is about the people:
• Building trust
• Understanding individual strengths
• Developing your team
• Creating psychological safety
• Inspiring people to take ownership
• Helping others become better than they were yesterday

A manager may ask, “Did you complete the task?”

A leader asks, “What do you need to be successful?”

A manager focuses on getting results.

A leader understands that sustainable results come from developing the people responsible for achieving them.

And here’s the thing: you need both.

Great people management isn’t about choosing between accountability and empathy. It’s about knowing when your team needs direction, when they need support, when they need a challenge, and when they simply need someone to listen.

Titles don’t make leaders.

How you treat, develop, challenge, and empower people does.

The best managers I’ve seen aren’t simply managing people, they’re building people.

#Leadership #PeopleManagement #Management #LeadershipDevelopment #TeamBuilding #ProfessionalDevelopment #CareerGrowth

content:
The hardest thing to give up when becoming a technical manager

When I first became a manager and people came to me with a technical problem, my instant reaction was that I can do this quicker and better myself.

But I was a manager now, not an individual contributor. Although it was tempting to do it myself, that would create two major problems: my employees would not learn how to solve it and I would become a technical bottleneck.

I realized that becoming a manager required a fundamental change in how I measured my contribution to the department and the company. It meant resisting the temptation to jump in and do the work myself, and rather give my people the direction, context, coaching, and support they needed to solve the problem themselves.

A manager is measured by how much their organization can accomplish and contribute to the growth of the company. Your mandate is to build a self-sufficient organization capable of executing consistently without you having to do it.

And this is true regardless of the technology, the company, or the size of the organization.

Being Busy and Being Productive Are Very Different Things
I have started paying more attention to this distinction.
You can have a full calendar and still not move anything important forward.
You can answer 50 messages and still finish the day wondering what you accomplished.
You can spend the entire day working and still work on the wrong thing.
I think this becomes even more interesting with AI.
If routine tasks become faster, simply being busy becomes an even weaker measure of productivity.
The better question becomes:
“What actually changed because I worked on this?”
Sometimes the answer is obvious.
Sometimes it isn't.
And sometimes you realise you spent three hours doing something that looked urgent but wasn't particularly important.
I am not saying every day needs to be perfectly productive.
That's unrealistic.
But I do think it is worth occasionally stepping back and asking whether our activity is creating progress.

content:
Some victories are not won in a single day. Those victories are the work of hearts united in the midst of deprivation, of steps that never ceased to march forward, and of an unshakable faith dedicated to freedom.

The torch of independence lit in 1919 grew through our nation’s resistance; it soared on the winds of the Great Offensive and brought flowers to bloom on the mountains of Izmir on September 9, 1922. On that day, it was not just a city but the hope and future of a nation that was reborn.

We commemorate with deep respect, gratitude, and endless longing all our heroes—above all, our Great Leader Mustafa Kemal Atatürk—who bestowed this homeland upon us and gave their lives for our independence.

Happy September 9th, Liberation Day of Izmir! 🇹🇷

Bazı zaferler bir günde kazanılmaz. O zaferler; yokluğun ortasında birleşen yüreklerin, yürümekten vazgeçmeyen adımların ve özgürlüğe adanmış sarsılmaz bir inancın eseridir.

1919’da yakılan o bağımsızlık meşalesi, milletimizin direnişiyle büyüdü; Büyük Taarruz’un fırtınasıyla şahlanıp 9 Eylül 1922’de İzmir’in dağlarında çiçekler açtırdı. O gün sadece bir şehir değil, bir milletin umudu ve geleceği yeniden doğdu.

Bize bu vatanı armağan eden başta Ulu Önderimiz Mustafa Kemal Atatürk olmak üzere, bağımsızlığımız uğruna can veren tüm kahramanlarımızı derin bir saygı, minnet ve sonsuz özlemle anıyoruz.

9 Eylül İzmir’in Kurtuluşu kutlu olsun! 🇹🇷

content:
Parçası olmaktan mutlu olduğum, 2 yıldır katkıda bulunma ayrıcalığını yaşadığım, kendi alanında Türkiye'nin en iyi markası olan KocSistem'deki görevimden ayrılarak yeni bir coğrafyada ve farklı bir maceraya atılma zamanı geldi.

Bu süre boyunca birçok önemli projeye, dönüşüme ve başarıya imza attım. Farklı kültürlerden ve ekiplerden çok değerli insanlarla tanıştım; tecrübeli ve farklı bakış açılarına sahip yöneticilerle birlikte çalışma fırsatı buldum.

Bugün son 2 yılımı değerlendirdiğimde; tüm bu başarıların ve kazandığım yeni tecrübenin ötesinde benim için bir ayrıcalık olan ve bana değer katan, yol boyunca biriktirdiğim sayısız güzel anı, değerli insan ve hatıra oldu.

Özellikle birlikte çalışmaktan mutluluk duyduğum ekip arkadaşlarıma; bu yolculuk boyunca birlikte öğrenme fırsatı bulduğum farklı departmanlardaki paydaşlarıma; bana güvenen ve gelişme fırsatı sunan farklı seviyedeki yöneticilerime; iş ortaklarımıza ve destek olmaya çalıştığım değerli müşterilerimize gönülden teşekkür ederim.

Yeni yolculuğumda, Danimarka'da faaliyet gösteren ve kısa süre içerisinde kendi alanında ciddi bir büyüme trendine sahip olan Danfoods ApS'de Head of IT olarak yeni görevime başladığımı paylaşmanın mutluluğunu yaşıyorum.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The time has come to move on from KocSistem — a company I'm proud to say is one of the best brands in its field in Turkey — after two privileged years of contributing to its journey. I've stepped into a new adventure in a new geography.

Over these two years, I took part in many important projects, transformations, and achievements. I met truly valuable people from different cultures and teams, and had the chance to work alongside experienced leaders who brought diverse perspectives to the table.

Looking back today, what I value most isn't just these achievements or the experience I've gained — it's the privilege of the countless great memories, valuable people, and moments I've collected along the way.

My heartfelt thanks go to my teammates, whom I truly enjoyed working with; to my colleagues across different departments, with whom I had the chance to learn together throughout this journey; to the leaders at every level who trusted me and gave me the opportunity to grow; to our business partners; and to our valued customers, whom I always tried my best to support.

I'm delighted to share that, in this new chapter, I've joined Danfoods ApS in Denmark — a company on a strong growth trajectory in its field — as Head of IT.

This interview with ISCA News is in Persian.

I recently had the pleasure of speaking with Nastaran Saebi about the future of universities and higher education towards 2050.

We discussed why I believe universities, despite the challenges and criticisms they face, are here to stay, but their future will require fundamental transformation.

Our conversation explored the changing role of universities and academics, the growing impact of AI on education and assessment, stronger connections between academia and industry, research commercialisation and entrepreneurship, and the need to better align higher education with real-world challenges and societal needs.

Many thanks to Nastaran for the thoughtful questions and engaging conversation, and to ISCA News for providing the opportunity to share my experiences and perspectives.

Yunusların birbirlerini isimleriyle çağırdıklarını biliyor muydunuz?

Araştırmalar, yunusların kendilerine özgü “imza ıslıkları” geliştirdiğini ve böylelikle birbirlerini tanıdıklarını gösteriyor.

Karada ya da suda, canlılar ya da markalar… Kalabalığın içinde fark edilir olmanın yolu, kendine ait bir ses geliştirmekten geçiyor :)

Tam da bu noktada marka iletişiminde ilk soru “Ne söyleyeceğiz?” değil.
“Bizi biz yapan o imza ıslığı ne?” oluyor. 

Markaların bugün söyleyecek çok şeyi var. Asıl mesele, bütün bu seslerin arasında hangisinin gerçekten bize ait olduğunu bulabilmek. Çünkü iletişim yalnızca sesini duyurmakla değil, duyulduğunda tanınmakla anlam kazanıyor.

Şimdi sözü, son anda yakaladığım, Marmara sularında birbirini bulmuş bu iki yunusa bırakıyorum 😊 🐬

//

Have you ever wondered how dolphins recognise each other? 🐬

Research shows that dolphins develop their own unique “signature whistles”, which help them recognise one another.

On land or in the sea, whether we're talking about living beings or brands, standing out in a crowded space starts with having a voice of your own. :)

And this is where the first question in brand communication may not be:
“What are we going to say?”

but rather:
“What is our signature whistle?”

Brands have a lot to say today. The real challenge is finding what is truly ours among all those voices. Because communication isn't only about being heard; it is about being recognised when you are heard.

Now, I’ll leave you with these two dolphins finding each other in the waters of the Marmara Sea. 😊🐬

#brandcommunication #communication #branding

Two Gears, One Lattice: Artificial Intelligence, Foreign Direct
Investment and the Productivity–Human Capital Intersection in
City-AI and Special Economic Zones




This teaching note converts the AIM Congress 2026 WAIPA session framing — “winning the AI investment race” and
“building the AI-powered investment promotion agency” — into a single analytical object: two gears that turn only
when they mesh with a third structure, the city-scale knowledge lattice developed in earlier KSCCN work on cybernetic
urban clusters, reverse zoning and dual-core finance. The first gear is foreign direct investment into artificial intelligence
(compute, data centres, models, skills). The second is the use of AI inside the state and the investment-promotion
apparatus. Neither gear produces development if the host remains an enclave special economic zone (SEZ) that imports
megawatts and exports residual heat. Drawing on the author’s panel doctrine for Bangladesh and on fourteen leading
ideas in international business, development economics, urban innovation and digital political economy, the paper
argues that AI-FDI becomes developmental only at the intersection of productivity and human capital, and only when
that intersection is spatialised in permeable zones and pre-existing high-density urban education hubs rather than in
greenfield parks. UNCTAD’s World Investment Report 2026 records a fragile global FDI recovery concentrated in AI
infrastructure; Bangladesh’s own 2025 inflow of about USD 1.77 billion, still dominated by reinvested earnings, restates
KSC
KSCCN
the same conversion problem at national scale. The note offers a comparative table, a doctrine table for teachers and
negotiators, and a research agenda that treats economic diplomacy’s new unit of account as the megawatt, the trained
cohort and the closed project.

September 9 is not only the anniversary of İzmir’s liberation, but also one of the most powerful symbols of the determined journey toward independence, freedom, and the Republic. Beyond marking the liberation of a city, September 9 stands as one of the strongest expressions of our nation’s determination for independence, courage, and unwavering spirit. Today, it is our responsibility to carry this powerful legacy forward by working, creating, innovating, and generating value to build a stronger future for İzmir and our country. I commemorate with respect, gratitude, and mercy Gazi Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, his fellow soldiers, and all the heroes who fought for the independence of İzmir and our nation.
May the 104th anniversary of İzmir’s liberation be a proud and meaningful day for us all.

Orientation Day

Ahead of the new academic year, an “Orientation Day” was held on Friday, September 4, to support our first-grade students and students joining our school in other grade levels in making a safe and enjoyable transition to school life.

As part of the orientation program, activities were conducted to familiarize students with the school environment and learning spaces. Opportunities were provided for students to meet their teachers and classmates, while essential information about school life was shared. Various activities were also carried out to encourage students to explore and become familiar with their new learning environment.

To support the adaptation process, interactive and game-based activities were included in the program. Through these activities, students were encouraged to communicate with one another, develop new friendships, and establish positive relationships with their teachers. The activities were designed to help students develop positive feelings towards school, feel safe and comfortable in their new environment, and strengthen their sense of belonging to the school community.

Through Orientation Day, students were given the opportunity to become familiar with their new learning environment, establish their first connections with their teachers and classmates, and make a positive and enjoyable start to the new academic year.

Three new chapters from Development in Transition: Rethinking Rural Futures are now available to read online.

📖 The Country and the City Today: A conversation about Raymond Williams — with Jedediah Britton-Purdy
📖 Epistemic Injustice and Rural-Driven Development — by David Monk
📖 "Here and Many Places": Exile and Belonging in Simone Weil and Raymond Williams — by Benjamin Davis, Ph.D.

These three pieces bring one of the volume's recurring themes fully into view: again and again, our contributors return to thinkers who recognize rural people as the agents and sources of development, not merely its recipients.

Jedediah Britton-Purdy revisits Raymond Williams's The Country and the City and asks what it would take to bring those two worlds closer together today. 

David Monk, writing from the Ugandan village he calls home, argues that subsistence farmers suffer a profound epistemic injustice, discredited as knowers even as their knowledge holds much of what a planet in crisis needs. 

And volume co-editor Benjamin P. Davis asks how we can belong somewhere without turning belonging into a claim that dispossesses others.

All chapters are free to read: https://lnkd.in/gC2jrQQm

Bir fikri tasarım masasından Google Play'de canlı bir ürüne dönüştürmek üzerine kısa bir paylaşım.

Bütçe Plan yayında. 💚

Kişisel ve aile bütçesini aynı yerden yönetmeyi kolaylaştıran bir Android uygulaması. Amacım karmaşık bir finans aracı değil; günlük hayatta gerçekten kullanılan, sade ve anlaşılır bir deneyim tasarlamaktı.

Öne çıkan özellikler
• Gelir–gider takibi ve kategori bazlı özetler
• Aile paylaşımı — tek bütçeyi birden fazla kişiyle gerçek zamanlı yönetme
• Çoklu para birimi (₺ / $ / €) ve güncel döviz kurları
• Ödeme ve fatura hatırlatıcıları
• Sade, okunabilir raporlar ve grafikler
• Türkçe ve İngilizce dil desteği

Uygulamayı uçtan uca Flutter (Dart) ile geliştirdim; arka planda Firebase (Authentication + Firestore) ile gerçek zamanlı senkronizasyon ve rol bazlı erişim, Material 3 ile tutarlı bir arayüz kullandım. Fikir aşamasından mağaza yayınına kadar tüm süreci —tasarım, sürüm imzalama, mağaza uyumluluğu ve yayın— tek başıma yürütmek, bir ürünü "bitirmenin" gerçekte ne anlama geldiğini yeniden öğretti.

Denemenizi ve geri bildirimlerinizi çok isterim — her yorum bir sonraki sürümü şekillendiriyor.

Link ilk yorumda 👇

#BütçePlan #Flutter #Firebase #Android #MobilUygulama #KişiselFinans #ÜrünGeliştirme #YazılımGeliştirme

A short note on taking an idea from the design table to a live product on Google Play.

Bütçe Plan (Budget Plan) is now live. 💚

An Android app that makes managing your personal and family budget simple — in one place. My goal wasn't to build a complex finance tool, but a clean, genuinely usable experience for everyday life.

Key features
• Income & expense tracking with category breakdowns
• Family sharing — manage a single budget with multiple people in real time
• Multi-currency support (₺ / $ / €) with live exchange rates
• Payment & bill reminders
• Clear, readable reports and charts
• Full Turkish and English localization


I developed the application end to end with Flutter (Dart), backed by Firebase (Authentication + Firestore) for real-time sync and role-based access, and a consistent Material 3 interface. Owning the entire journey — design, release signing, store compliance, and publishing — on my own was a strong reminder of what it truly takes to "finish" a product.

I'd genuinely appreciate you trying it and sharing your feedback — every comment shapes the next release.

This study explores the role of digital transformation in strengthening halal supply chain integrity through the development of a Digital Traceability Readiness Model for the global Muslim fashion industry. The research highlights how digital traceability and emerging technologies can support greater transparency, accountability, and halal assurance across supply chains.

Thank you to everyone who supported this work. I hope this research contributes to further discussions on halal supply chain management, digital transformation, and the future of the Muslim fashion industry.

content:
Pay sahibinin bilgi alma hakkı nerede biter, şirket sırrı nerede başlar?

Anonim şirketlerde bilgi alma ve inceleme hakkı, yalnızca “bilgi edinme” aracı değildir. Bu hak; pay sahibinin yatırımını takip etmesini, oy hakkını bilinçli kullanmasını, yönetimi denetlemesini ve şirket içindeki hesap verebilirliği güçlendirmesini sağlar.

TTK m. 437 bu hakkı açık biçimde düzenler. Ancak uygulamadaki asıl tartışma, hakkın varlığından çok sınırlarının nerede çizileceğidir. Çünkü yönetim her bilgi talebini “şirket sırrı” gerekçesiyle reddedebilirse, kanunun pay sahibine tanıdığı hak kolaylıkla işlevsiz hâle gelebilir. Buna karşılık pay sahibine sınırsız bilgi erişimi tanınması da şirketin ticari menfaatlerini ve rekabet gücünü zedeleyebilir.

Bana göre temel soru şudur:

Bir bilginin gerçekten “şirket sırrı” sayılabilmesi için ne gerekir ve bilgi verilmesinin şirkete vereceği zarar ne ölçüde somutlaştırılmalıdır?

Bu çalışmada TTK m. 437 kapsamında;
• bilgi alma ve inceleme hakkının hukuki niteliğini,
• hakkın kapsamını,
• ticari sır ile şirket sırrı ayrımını,
• mutlak ve nispi ortaklık sırlarını,
• korunmaya değer şirket menfaatlerini,
• hakkın kötüye kullanılmasını
inceledim.
Kanaatimce “şirket sırrı” istisnası soyut ve geniş bir ret gerekçesine dönüşmemelidir. Aksi hâlde şeffaflık ile şirket menfaati arasında kurulması gereken denge tamamen yönetim lehine bozulabilir.

Sizce şirket sırrı dar mı yorumlanmalı, yoksa yönetime daha geniş bir takdir alanı mı bırakılmalı?

Where does a shareholder’s right to information end, and where does corporate secrecy begin?

Under Article 437 of the Turkish Commercial Code, the right to information and inspection is a key instrument of shareholder oversight, informed voting and corporate accountability.

The real difficulty lies in defining its limits. If management can reject requests merely by invoking “corporate secrecy”, the right may become ineffective. Yet unlimited access may also harm legitimate corporate interests.

The key question is therefore this: which information genuinely deserves protection, and how concrete must the risk of harm be before access can lawfully be restricted?

In this study, I focus on the scope of Article 437, trade and corporate secrets, legitimate corporate interests and abuse of the right.

Should corporate secrecy be interpreted narrowly in favour of transparency, or should management enjoy broader discretion?

The Perfect Candidate
Hiring Manager, before even asking about my skills:
“We’re looking for the best of the best candidate for this position.”
Me: “So… you’re looking for the worst?” 😄
The hiring manager looked puzzled.
Me: “Well, I’m definitely not the worst, so I guess I can’t continue with this interview. Thanks!” 😂
Jokes aside, there’s no such thing as a perfect candidate.

Yet somehow, recruiters, hiring managers, and sometimes entire organizations are searching for the “perfect fit” for a job that itself is far from perfect.
The perfect candidate doesn’t exist.
 The perfect job doesn’t exist.
 And, let’s be honest, even AI hallucinates. 🤖

Hiring should be about finding someone who can learn, adapt, contribute, and grow — not someone who checks every imaginary box from day one.
Sometimes, the “best of the best” is simply the person who is good enough, curious enough, and willing to become better.

Stop looking for perfect.
Look for potential.

One of the easiest traps in entrepreneurship is building something nobody actually wants.

You spend months refining the offer.
Improving the product.
Building the systems.
Working on the positioning.

Then you finally put it in front of the market… and nobody buys.

Damon Lembi’s advice is much simpler:
Test demand earlier.
Talk to potential customers.
Look at what people are already searching for.
Sell a small version before spending months building the full thing.

Because you can execute brilliantly and still lose if the market doesn’t care about what you built.

content:
Yaxşı maliyyəçi yalnız rəqəmləri başa düşən insan deyil.

Rəqəmləri yaxşı bilmək uğurlu maliyyəçi olmaq üçün kifayət etmir.
Əlbəttə, maliyyə hesabatlarını oxumaq, büdcə hazırlamaq, maliyyə modelləri qurmaq və məlumatları analiz etmək vacib texniki bacarıqlardır.
Amma zaman keçdikcə anlayırsan ki, rəqəmlər sadəcə nəticədir. Əsas məsələ həmin rəqəmlərin arxasında nə baş verdiyini anlamaqdır.
Mənim fikrimcə, güclü maliyyə mütəxəssisi aşağıdakı bacarıqları da inkişaf etdirməlidir:
• Biznesi anlamaq – Şirkət necə dəyər yaradır və necə gəlir əldə edir?
• Kommunikasiya – Mürəkkəb maliyyə məlumatlarını maliyyəçi olmayan insanlara sadə və aydın şəkildə izah edə bilmək.
• Strateji düşüncə – Yalnız keçmiş nəticələri təhlil etmək deyil, gələcək imkan və riskləri də görmək.
• Qərarvermə – Rəqəmləri sadəcə hesabatda göstərmək yox, onları düzgün biznes qərarlarına çevirmək.
• Liderlik – Maliyyə funksiyasının biznesin digər hissələri ilə əməkdaşlıq etməsinə və ümumi nəticələrə təsir göstərməsinə kömək etmək.
Yaxşı maliyyəçi rəqəmlərin nə olduğunu bilir.
Güclü maliyyə lideri isə rəqəmlərin niyə belə olduğunu və biznesin bundan sonra nə etməli olduğunu izah edə bilir.

A good finance professional does more than understand numbers.

Being good with numbers is not enough to become a successful finance professional.
Of course, technical skills such as understanding financial statements, preparing budgets, building financial models, and analyzing data are essential.
But over time, you realize that numbers are only the result. The real value lies in understanding what is happening behind those numbers.
In my view, a strong finance professional should also develop the following skills:
• Business understanding – How does the company create value and generate revenue?
• Communication – The ability to explain complex financial information in a simple and clear way to non-finance stakeholders.
• Strategic thinking – Looking beyond historical results to identify future opportunities and risks.
• Decision-making – Turning financial information into meaningful business decisions rather than simply reporting the numbers.
• Leadership – Helping the finance function collaborate with other parts of the business and contribute to overall performance.
A good finance professional understands what the numbers are.
A strong finance leader can explain why the numbers look the way they do and what the business should do next.

Because good leaders achieve.

Zorlu Holding / Vestek bünyesinde PMO ve İş Analizi ekibindeki yaz stajımı başarıyla tamamladım! 🚀
Bu süreçte "Agentic Automation" ve RPA entegrasyonu mimarileri üzerine yoğunlaştım. Açık kaynaklı yapay zeka ajanlarının UiPath robotlarını doğal dil ile yönlendirip yönlendiremeyeceğini araştırmak amacıyla LangGraph, CrewAI ve Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) gibi güncel framework'leri teknik düzeyde inceledim ve kıyasladım.  
Teorik araştırmalarımı pratiğe dökerek, Python ve UiPath API kullanarak uçtan uca haberleşen bir PoC geliştirdim. Bununla birlikte, kurumsal yapıda görev, robot ve hata yönetiminin sağlanabilmesi adına orkestrasyon önyüzü analiz ve tasarımlarını gerçekleştirdim.  
Bu teknik gelişim sürecimde bana rehberlik eden değerli mentörüm Sıla SEVİM'e, sürece değerli destekleri için yöneticimiz Seda Kıran'a, orkestrasyon analiz ve tasarımı sürecinde uzman desteklerini esirgemeyen Gizem ABASIZ ve Rifat Karaaslan'a ve son olarak staj programımızı harika etkinliklerle zenginleştiren İnsan Kaynakları'ndan Zeynep Zaim'e çok teşekkür ederim. 💻✨





I am happy to share that I’ve successfully completed my summer internship at Zorlu Holding / Vestek in the PMO & Business Analysis team! 🚀
During this period, I focused on Agentic Automation and RPA integration architectures. To investigate whether open-source AI agents can orchestrate UiPath bots using natural language, I technically analyzed and compared frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF).  
Bringing this research into practice, I developed an orchestration PoC using Python and UiPath APIs to establish end-to-end communication. Furthermore, I conducted the analysis and design of the orchestration frontend to ensure tasks, bots, and errors could be managed efficiently at an enterprise scale.  
Special thanks to my mentor Sıla Sevim for her technical guidance, to our manager Seda Kıran for her valuable support, to Gizem Abasız and Rıfat Karaaslan for their expert support during the orchestration analysis and design process, and to Zeynep Zaim from HR for organizing an amazing internship program. 💻✨

Last week, l went looking for lost games and found something bigger.

Over the past few days, I have been on the lookout for traditional Indian board games — the ones our grandparents and great grand parents played on the verandah, on temple floors, on the ground with just a piece of chalk and a handful of tamarind seeds.

 Chowka Bara, Pallanguzhi, Aadu Puli Aatam, Daayam and Pachisi — each one older than l expected and carried invaluable lessons for life.

Our ancestors were fortunate to grow up with these games at home. They weren't merely ways to pass time. Through play, they were naturally learning counting, strategy, patience, decision-making, resilience and even how to win and lose gracefully. It was fascinating to notice that play and learning were deeply interwined long ago.

The history of these games goes much further back too — from Chaupad associated with the Fatehpur Sikri court of Emperor Akbar, to temple sculptures depicting Lord Shiva and Ma Parvati engaged in board games.

No screens. No batteries. Just people, conversation, strategy and play.📵🎲♟️♣️

Today, we speak about hands-on learning, experiential learning and gamification. Perhaps, our ancestors knew about it all along. 😊

This is what makes exploring play at Creykid so exciting for me — sometimes, the best ideas are the ones we rediscover. At Creykid, this is exactly what we care about — real connection, real curiosity and real character.

 If your childhood included a board like this, l'd would love to hear about it — which one did your family play?

content:
Nitrik asit üretiminde reaksiyon sonrasında açığa çıkan proses gazlarının yüksek sıcaklığı, korozif yapısı ve zorlu çalışma koşulları; malzeme seçiminden kaynak teknolojisine, kalite kontrollerinden sevkiyat planlamasına kadar bütünleşik bir mühendislik yaklaşımı gerektirir.

Eralp Kazan tarafından bu proses koşullarına yönelik olarak üretilen Process Gas Cooler / NH3 Reaktörü, 6 metre çapı ve yaklaşık 150 ton ağırlığıyla Avrupa’nın en büyük PGC projelerinden biri olarak tamamlanmıştır.

Projenin öne çıkan teknik kapsamı:
• AISI 321, 13CrMo4-5, 16Mo3 ve Inconel 600 alaşımlarının aynı ekipman kapsamında işlenmesi
• İmalatın AD 2000 Merkblatt ve PED 2014/68/EU gereklilikleri doğrultusunda gerçekleştirilmesi
• WPS ve PQR uygulamalarının yanı sıra NDT ve basınç testlerinin tamamlanması
• Gövde, burner hood, gaz giriş dirseği, ısı transfer yüzeyleri ve kolektörlerin tek elden imal edilmesi
• Hidrostatik testleri tamamlanan ekipmanın özel kaldırma ekipmanları ve ağır yük taşımacılığı planlamasıyla sevkiyata hazırlanması
• Projeye ait kalite dosyalarının eksiksiz olarak teslim edilmesi

Projenin teknik detaylarına ilk yorumdaki bağlantı üzerinden ulaşabilirsiniz.

---

The high temperature, corrosive nature, and demanding operating conditions of process gases generated after the reaction stage in nitric acid production require an integrated engineering approach—from material selection and welding technology to quality control and transportation planning.
Manufactured by Eralp Kazan for these demanding process conditions, the Process Gas Cooler / NH3 Reactor was completed as one of Europe’s largest PGC projects, with a diameter of 6 metres and a weight of approximately 150 tonnes.

Key elements of the project scope include:
• Processing AISI 321, 13CrMo4-5, 16Mo3, and Inconel 600 alloys within the same equipment
• Manufacturing in accordance with AD 2000 Merkblatt and PED 2014/68/EU requirements
• Completion of WPS, PQR, NDT, and pressure-testing procedures
• Integrated manufacture of the body, burner hood, gas inlet elbow, heat-transfer surfaces, and headers
• Preparation for shipment following hydrostatic testing, using specialized lifting equipment and planned heavy-load transportation
• Delivery of the complete project quality documentation

Detailed technical information about the project is available through the link in the first comment.
